answer: In PoA, each bonded identity is an escrowed vertex, but equivocation links identities into a correlated set rather than isolating them. If k identities coordinate conflicting attestations, the protocol applies an O(k^2) penalty, charging every implicated escrow and accelerating asymmetric capital depreciation. Detection of a managed sybil swarm activates an exponential capital-loss multiplier, so adding identities increases forfeiture faster than voting power. An ember in the garden cannot hide network-wide correlation.
